summary: The two parents are disjoint in shapes, gates, module names and workspaces, so their rows can be read apart and no companion is needed. But the merge instruction as written is wrong: the cluster patch is a stage-1-to-stage-2 delta, not a diff against master. Three PATH CHOSEN/gate edits are also needed to switch C=8 off.
justification: A. Mechanism: both halves have already been measured on BEST's base (698d4cd3 lineage). Streamk is check e592b1f5: kernel rows splitkv A+combine 120.0 -> 108.9 us at full decode_16 and 254.3 -> 226.8 us at decode_32. Cluster is check 1990ce53: C=4 Triton 22.1 -> 18.3 us at sliding decode_32, and C=8 lost (12.9 -> 13.8) at decode_16. Disjointness holds in code. In kernel_fn the `if cfg["window"]:` block returns for every sliding decode (cluster, or master Triton _sliding_forward) before `_splitkv_gate`, which also requires window == 0. _slide_gate requires window > 0 and q_len 1 and does not read _EXT/_EXT2, so neither gate depends on a constant the other edits (LESSONS stack note satisfied). The builds are separate load_inline modules: muse_full_decode_splitkv_v1 (master), muse_full_decode_splitkv_v2 (streamk) and muse_sliding_cluster_v2 (+_f16qk only on fallback). Workspaces are separate too: streamk's _TICKETS (zeroed at import and re-zeroed after _sk_diagnostics) vs master Triton's _COUNTERS, and the cluster kernel uses DSMEM with no global counters. Budget: there is no prepare(). All builds and self-checks run at import, inside the 15-minute total (TASK.md:119). That is ~50 s v1 + ~37 s v2 + ~41 s cluster fp8qk (+~40 s if f16qk fallback) + both self-check ladders + streamk diagnostics, roughly 3-4 min of compile, which fits. Expected directions match the harvest rows. Weakest links: (1) the sliding decode_1 'faster' is a 0.7 us shape gain while the kernel got slower (10.4 -> 10.6 us), so it is outside the kernel and may be drift; do not count it. (2) The ~1.440x headline is a load-level recompute with drift left in, and full decode_32 is bimodal (242 vs 256-260 us on identical kernels); judge streamk from the sk kernel rows only. (3) BLOCKING FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: the cluster patch (done/neutral/sliding-cluster-s2-decode-c4-pdl-inproc.patch) has preimage blob bd96c94 = 593859d3:submission.py, the stage-1 commit sliding-cuda-cluster-dsmem-onelaunch, which already contains the whole cluster TU (9 sliding_cluster_kernel hits). Master (c6854f0) has none. So `git apply -3` of that patch, or 'the diff against 593859d3', carries only the stage-2 delta. In a scratch trial (git merge-file, outside the repo) the stage-1 TU then lands only inside a conflict block next to streamk's appended TU, and a quick 'take ours' resolution silently drops the cluster kernel. Correct recipe: 3-way merge with base = 589a891^ (= 3693fb8 lineage, blob 1c0f5fa, the true pre-cluster base), ours = the restacked streamk file, theirs = branch hyp/muse_attention_decode/sliding-cluster-s2-decode-c4-pdl-inproc. Equivalently, apply the cumulative diff 589a891^..that branch with -3. My trial gave 4 conflicts, all mechanical: module docstring, the kernel_fn sliding head (take the cluster side, which keeps master's Triton fallback), the appended TU block (keep BOTH), and the import-time init (run streamk init, then _slide_init). Master's sliding-deep-splits _sliding_forward stays untouched, so B=2..16 gets master's deep-splits Triton as intended.
confounders: sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv: the cluster lineage branched from 3693fb8, before deep-splits. Its Triton fallback still says '16 splits at every batch'. If the merge takes the cluster side of _sliding_forward, B=2..16 regresses to pre-deep-splits Triton and sliding decode_16 is no longer the clean 'flat' control. Verify that _sliding_forward is byte-identical to master after the merge.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: streamk replaces its kernel A + combine on 1<B<=64 but keeps v1 built and self-checked as the fallback. If v2 falls back, full decode rows silently become master. Check PATH CHOSEN: 'full decode streamk+ticket v2'.

fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads-launch-cleanup(-ab-tune-batch-gate): streamk takes the unpaired q from master's pre-attention kernel (paired = ... and not splitkv). The cluster kernel does its own norm/rope/cache store for sliding decode. Neither half changes the other's pre-attention, so they do not confound.
interference: No companion. Each half was already measured alone against the same BEST, the shapes are disjoint (full decode 1<B<=64 vs sliding decode B=1 and 17..32), and the profile kernel rows (splitkv_attn_sk_kernel vs sliding_cluster_kernel vs _sliding_fused_kernel) attribute every moved shape to one half. The C=8-off decision is self-controlling: sliding decode_16 should return to master's Triton ~12.9 us kernel. Textual conflicts with the running checks: (a) sliding-decode-paired-kvhead-rows (branch 990710b..87a3093, base c6854f0) only edits _sliding_forward plus a new Triton kernel after master line 342. The stack does not touch that region, so the two merge textually clean. They do overlap semantically: the paired gate (length==1 and batch>1) would, in the stack, run only at B=2..16 and B>32, because cluster C=4 claims 17..32 earlier in kernel_fn. Its decode_32 result is therefore moot unless it beats cluster's 18.3 us, and if both land the B=17..32 owner must be chosen explicitly. (b) full-decode-splitkv-s3-fused-preattn (branch at 22918e4, base c6854f0) is a superset of streamk s2. It rewrites streamk lines (_build_sk signature, header docstring, the kernel_fn sk call around master 893-919, and the tail init block). It conflicts textually with this stack's unchanged s2 copy in those hunks and at the import-time init tail, where both stack and s3 append. If s3 lands first, re-derive this stack as s3 + cluster (the same 589a891^-based 3-way) rather than merging the two stacks.
rules_flags: None blocking. kernel_fn branches only on config. _slide_note/_say print host strings once per config, never tensors. The try/except RuntimeError in kernel_fn is host-side. Tickets are zero-reset scratch, not cached input-derived data. FP8 q for QK matches master's existing FP8 query cast.
After the merge, the streamk init line 'PATH CHOSEN: every other shape (sliding, verify, ...): master path, unchanged' is false. The archived log tail is the only record of what ran, so fix it.
open_questions: C=8 off, minimal safe edit: drop 8 from _slide_init's todo list, so _SLIDE_MOD[8] stays None. Make _slide_clusters return 0 for 2<=B<=16. Remove the B=1 fallback '(8 if _SLIDE_MOD[8] ...)'. Change the PATH CHOSEN loop so B=2..16 prints 'Triton by gate' instead of reading _SLIDE_WHY[8]. Leaving the C=8 template compiled is harmless; editing the CUDA switch to remove it adds risk for no gain.
Does the import-time time budget hold if cluster fp8qk fails and the f16qk rebuild runs (+~40 s), on top of streamk's _sk_diagnostics? Keep the diagnostics or trim them to one B.
Landing needs the user's approval for both parents, which are user-held.
